column2: Seeing his body worn out by old age and the like, O best of men, he should entrust his wife to his sons or take her with him and go to the forest.
He should bathe three times a day, wear his nails, beard and matted locks, sleep on the ground, be celibate, and be devoted to the five sacrifices;
always eat fruits and roots, delight in study, be compassionate to all beings and devoted to Narayana.
He should avoid flowers and fruits grown in villages, eat only eight mouthfuls, and not eat at night.
A forest-dweller should avoid oil entirely; he should avoid sexual union, and also sleep and sloth.
He should always remember Narayana with conch, discus and mace in hand; the forest-dweller should practise austerities such as the Chandrayana.
He should bear cold, heat and the like, and always tend the fire. When detachment from all things arises in the mind,
then, O Brahmin, he should renounce; otherwise he falls. Devoted to the study of Vedanta, peaceful, self-controlled, master of senses,
he should always be free of dualities, ego and possessiveness, endowed with peace and the other qualities, free of desire and anger.
The twice-born ascetic should be naked or wear a worn loincloth, with shaven head; equal to foe and friend, to honour and dishonour.
He should stay one night in a village and three nights in a town; he should live always by alms and not eat the food of one house.
The ascetic should go for alms to the house of a blameless Brahmin, when the fire is out, meals are done, and there is no quarrel.
He should bathe three times a day, be devoted to Narayana, and constantly chant Om, with self and senses conquered.
An ascetic who sometimes eats the food of one house and is greedy has no atonement even with ten thousand penances.
If an ascetic, O Brahmin, out of greed devotes himself to nourishing his body, he should be known as equal to a Chandala, censured by all classes and orders.
He should contemplate the Self as God Narayana, faultless, free of dualities and possessiveness, peaceful, beyond maya, without envy,
imperishable, complete, whose sole form is perpetual bliss, of the nature of knowledge, stainless, the supreme eternal light,
changeless, without beginning or end, the cause of the consciousness of the world, without qualities; he should meditate on the Self as the highest of the high.
He should recite Upanishad texts and reflect on the meaning of Vedanta; with senses conquered he should always meditate on the thousand-headed God.
The ascetic who, devoted to meditation thus and free of envy, goes to supreme bliss, the supreme eternal light.
The twice-born who follows the duties of the orders of life in order thus goes to the highest place, from which he does not grieve.
Those devoted to the duties of class and order of life, free of all sins and devoted to Narayana, go to the supreme abode of Vishnu.
He should remember the god Narayana, infinite and unconquered; he should recite the Vaishnava verses, the demon-destroying ones, and especially those for the ancestors.
He should recite the Purusha hymn, the three Nachiketa fires, the Trimadhu, Trisuparna, Pavamana and Yajus texts;
and he should speak merit-giving common ancestral texts, the epics, Puranas and dharma-scriptures,
for as long as the Brahmins eat, O Brahmin. When the Brahmins have eaten, he should scatter the vikira offering,
speak of the remaining food, and recite the Madhu hymn. Having washed his own feet and properly sipped water, O Narada,
when the Brahmins have sipped water, he should offer the balls. He should say the auspicious blessing and "akshayya" water,
and having given them attentively, make the salutation to the Brahmins. Those twice-born who say the blessing without moving the dish
— for a year their ancestors become eaters of leavings. With "May our givers prosper" and similar texts declared by Smriti,
he should receive their blessings and then bow; he should give a fee as he can and betel with perfume.
Having brought an inverted vessel, he should utter "svadha", and with the verse "vaje vaje" dismiss the ancestors and gods.
The eater, and the performer of shraddha, should avoid sexual union that night, and also study and travel with effort.
A traveller, a sick man, or one lacking wealth should perform shraddha with raw grain, or with gold if he has no wife (or "grass").
Lacking materials or Brahmins, he should cook just food; the wise man should make oblation with the ancestral hymn.
If entirely without offerings, he should, as able, give grass to cows, or, having bathed properly, offer sesame-and-water.
Or he may weep very loudly in a lonely forest, saying, "I am poor, a great sinner."
A man who performs shraddha but does not offer to the ancestors the next day: his family goes to ruin and he incurs Brahmin-slaying.
Men who perform shraddha with faith, O lord of sages, have no break in progeny and become prosperous.
Those who worship the ancestors in shraddha have worshipped Vishnu; when the Lord of the world is pleased, all the gods are pleased.
The ancestors, the gods, Gandharvas, Apsarases, Yakshas, Siddhas, men — all are Hari, the eternal.
From whom all this world, moving and unmoving, was born — therefore the giver and the eater are Vishnu, the eternal, all.
Whatever exists, O Brahmin, whatever does not, the seen and the unseen — know all to be made of Vishnu; nothing else exists.
The support of the universe, the Self of all beings, imperishable, of incomparable nature, the Lord who enjoys offerings to gods and ancestors,
the one who is called Supreme Brahman is Janardana alone, doer and causer; Vishnu, the eternal, is all.
Thus, best of sages, the supreme rule of shraddha has been told to you; for those who do so, sin dissolves at once.
The best of twice-born who reads this with devotion at the time of shraddha pleases his ancestors, and his progeny increases.
For those who bathe, give and chant at the time, there is imperishable fruit. There, the Karka (Cancer) transit is known as the southern course (dakshinayana).
The wise know that the thirty ghatikas before it are the meritorious time. In Taurus, Scorpio, Leo and Aquarius,
the eight muhurtas before are to be taken for bathing, chanting and the like; in Libra and Aries, before and after,
ten ghatikas are known to make gifts imperishable. In Virgo, Gemini, Pisces and Sagittarius, O Brahmin,
sixteen ghatikas after are known to give merit. The Makara (Capricorn) transit is called the northern course (uttarayana);
forty ghatikas after, as before; thirty after as well. If the sun and cool-rayed moon are to be taken as set,
having bathed, he should eat, O best of Brahmins, on the next day in a pure circle. The new moon seen with the moon is Sinivali; with the moon lost, Kuhu.
The wise who seek dharma speak of the new moon in two kinds. Sinivali is to be taken by the twice-born who keep fires in shraddha rites;
Kuhu by women, Shudras and those without fires. If the new-moon tithi spans two afternoons,
in case of decrease, the earlier is to be taken; in increase, the later. If the new moon is known to extend beyond noon,
it is called "bhuta-viddha" by scripture experts. In case of extreme decrease, the next day does not reach the afternoon;
there Sinivali, the tithi extending to the evening, is to be taken; and in a later decrease likewise the tithi extending to the evening,
the later Sinivali is to be taken in every case for shraddha. In extreme increase of the tithi, one should leave the one touched by the 14th (bhuta);
for ancestral rites Kuhu in the afternoon should be taken; in later increase, those joined with bhuta are to be abandoned.
On the next day, the best of the wise take Kuhu that extends to the afternoon. If the new-moon tithi spans both middays,
there either the earlier or the later may be taken at will. Now I shall tell the anvadhana (laying of fire) at the full moon, O good one.
He should perform the sacrifice on the first day; the first quarter of the parvan and the first three days
are known as the time of the sacrifice, called the morning time by the wise. If new and full moon span both middays,
O best of Brahmins, the next day itself is prescribed as the immediate time.
If it is in the earlier two, the next day after the sangava period; the immediate time is the next day, thus to be known in decrease of tithi.
All should take the eleventh (ekadashi) free of the tenth; the eleventh joined with the tenth destroys the merit gained in three births.
If the eleventh is a mere digit and is found at the twelfth, and the twelfth at the thirteenth, the later is held to be higher.
If the full eleventh, pure, is found also on the twelfth, and the thirteenth at the night's end, here I shall give the decision:
the earlier is for householders and the later for ascetics; householders seek success, ascetics liberation.
If the breaking of the fast can be had on the twelfth, even a digit, then the eleventh, though joined with the tenth, is to be fasted.
If there are two elevenths in a bright or dark half, the earlier is for householders and the later for ascetics.
If a part of the twelfth is present joined with the tenth, at the decrease of the day, the second alone is declared for all.
An eleventh joined with the tenth is to be taken if the twelfth does not follow; even a pure one is forbidden if the twelfth follows.
